Welcome to the course repository for the Graduate Computational Social Networks Sequence (SOCIOL 208A & 208B) at UCLA. This website hosts all syllabi, reading schedules, interactive lecture notes, R code snippets, and instructional materials.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}

::: {.card-body}
### <i class="bi bi-laptop"></i> SOCIOL 208A {.card-title .text-primary}
**Social Networks Methods**  
*Fall Quarter*

A graduate-level seminar focused on the data-analytic and computational techniques used in Social Network Analysis (SNA). This course covers the practical application of network theory using `R` and `igraph`.

**Key Topics Covered:**
<ul class="list-unstyled">
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Centrality, status, and prestige measures</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Cohesion, equivalence, and similarity</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Community detection and subgroups</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Two-mode (bipartite) networks</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Statistical models (ERGM, QAP, Swapping)</li>
</ul>

::: {.d-flex .gap-2 .mt-3}

### <i class="bi bi-people"></i> SOCIOL 208B {.card-title .text-primary}
**Social Networks Theory**  
*Spring Quarter*

A substantive graduate seminar exploring the theories, perspectives, and empirical research in sociology through a social networks lens. The focus is on substantive contributions and conceptual frameworks.

**Key Topics Covered:**
<ul class="list-unstyled">
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Relational sociology & network thinking</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Weak ties, homophily, and brokerage</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Collaboration networks & field dynamics</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Network diffusion and contagion</li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short text-primary"></i> Historical social networks & inequality</li>
</ul>

::: {.d-flex .gap-2 .mt-3}

### Sequence Overview

The sequence is designed to equip students with both the theoretical foundations and the methodological toolkit required to conduct original, publication-quality research using network analytic approaches:

```{mermaid}
%%| theme: neutral
flowchart LR
    A[SOCIOL 208A: Methods] -->|Methodological Toolkit| C(Original Research)
    B[SOCIOL 208B: Theory] -->|Theoretical Foundations| C
```

To get started, select a course syllabus from the cards above or browse the lecture topics directly using the sidebar navigation.
